newsitem.title: UK: London Electricity firm after dip in profit.
newsitem.headline: London Electricity firm after dip in profit.

text.p: Shares in regional UK power company London Electricity were higher in pre-market trade on Thursday despite a fall in half-year pretax profits.
The shares were up 4p at 644p by 0816 GMT.
London Electricity said half-year pretax profits had dropped to 69.3 million stg, down from 84.5 million stg last year, but profits came within analysts' forecasts of 61.7-86 million stg.

"Our first-half trading results were, as anticipated, affected by the tougher regulatory regime following the two distribution reviews," said chairman Bob Reid. Distribution revenues were reduced by 6.2 million stg to 155.3 million stg.

The company said investment in its distribution networks remained the priority but added that the proposed tax changes announced in the Budget would necessitate a re-examination of the company's investment strategy.
The interim dividend was raised to 14.3 pence/shr, up from 11.5 pence previously and towards the top end of expectations.
